title: Test Administrator (TIMSS) - Wales - Fully Remote
description:
Background

Pearson is responsible for the delivery of the TIMSS international assessment study in schools in Wales.

The Trends in Maths and Science Study (TIMSS) is an international comparative study that assesses and compares the performance in maths and science of pupils at age 10, or Y5 in Wales, every four years across about 60 countries. It provides internationally comparative data on pupils' achievement in maths and science, and how their performance is related to their attitudes, gender and background . More information on the study is available online:

Pearson is recruiting external Test Administrators (TAs) to administer this study in schools in Wales.

The pupil assessment is split into two test sections followed by a questionnaire section. Test Administrators will need to be confident using technology however, training will be given on accessing and using the online platform. Schools are also asked to have an IT technician available on the day. Online remote TA training is mandatory to ensure standardisation in the delivery of the study's requirements.
Purpose

Test Administrators administer pupil assessments and questionnaires online within designated schools, ensuring that the international procedures are adhered to in full. Successful applicants for this role will be trained remotely on the procedures and must complete pre-training activities and attend a live training/Q&A session in the two to three weeks prior to the test window. Preparation for the training session will include reading the TA manual and completing short online assessments on aspects of the pre-training materials.
Main Responsibilities
- Liaise with the School Coordinator or Headteacher regarding arrangements for the test day, such as room bookings and desk/table layout of the room/s to be used and access to IT facilities, as needed.
- Ensure there are enough computers / laptops on the assessment day for all pupils.
- Ensure that pupils are sitting their assigned assessment.
- Administer the assessments and pupil questionnaire in accordance with international standards as outlined in the training and instructions provided, maintaining test security at all times.
- Ensure the correct timing of the sessions, recording the session start and end times.
- Record pupil participation and complete appropriate administrative paperwork as outlined in training.
- After completion of the pupil assessments and questionnaires, ensure administration documents are returned to Pearson.
- Ensure schools are reminded that teacher and school questionnaires need to be completed by the test date.
- Set up and administer devices supplied by Pearson (laptops), in schools where this is needed, following the guidance given.
Relevant Experience
- Experience of teaching and / or working in a school classroom.
- Confident using IT applications, particularly for onscreen assessment.
- Experience of invigilating tests / examinations.
Competencies Required
- Ability to adhere to specified procedural standards.
- Confident troubleshooting common technology user issues.
- Excellent verbal communication skills.
- Good organisation and administrative skills.
- Ability to identify, communicate and escalate issues promptly and effectively.
- Ability to work to agreed timeframes.
Essential Requirements
- Availability for the study as per the following:

o remote TA training 29 Apr 2027 15:00 - 17:30

o test window 17 May to 2 Jul 2027 Mon to Fri to visit c. 2-3 schools per week
- Arrival time at school is usually 08.00 and finish time is approximately 13.00 (agreed with individual schools depending on local circumstances).
- Car and driving licence for travel to schools, as required (use of public transport is encouraged, where practical).
- If successful, we will apply for an Enhanced DBS certificate for you, covering working with children.
- Commitment to the safeguarding and welfare of all pupils.
Desirable Requirements

Overnight stays may occasionally be necessary to be at the school by 08.00.

Ability to deliver in the Welsh language will expand the number of potential schools you can visit.

title: School Administrator
description:
Job Title: School Administrator
Responsible to: Headteacher / School Business Manager
Salary Grade: 92 - 100 a day
Hours: School ter times
Contract: Temporary

1. Job Purpose

To provide an efficient, professional and effective administrative service, supporting the day-to-day operation of the school. The postholder will support the Headteacher, staff, pupils, parents/carers and governors, contributing to the school's vision, values and commitment to improving learner outcomes, wellbeing and inclusion.

The role will support Welsh Government education priorities, including the Curriculum for Wales, safeguarding, Additional Learning Needs (ALN), equality and inclusion, and the promotion of Welsh language and culture.

2. Key Duties and Responsibilities

The School Administrator will:
- Provide a welcoming, professional first point of contact for parents/carers, pupils, visitors, staff and external agencies.
- Manage telephone calls, emails, correspondence and general enquiries, ensuring information is communicated accurately and promptly.
- Provide administrative support to the Headteacher, senior leadership team, teaching staff and governors.
- Maintain accurate and up-to-date pupil records, staff information and school management information systems.
- Support pupil admissions, transfers, leavers and transition arrangements.
- Record and monitor pupil attendance, follow up unexplained absences and produce attendance reports.
- Prepare letters, newsletters, reports, presentations, meeting papers and other school documentation.
- Organise meetings, appointments, school events, trips and visits.
- Support financial administration, including processing orders, invoices, payments and purchase requisitions in accordance with school procedures.
- Maintain effective filing, record-keeping and document management systems, ensuring information is stored securely.

3. Person Specification

Essential:
- Good standard of general education, including English and Mathematics, or equivalent experience.
- Experience in an administrative or customer-facing role.
- Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office.
- Excellent organisational, communication and time-management skills.
- Ability to maintain accurate records and handle confidential information.
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

Desirable:
- Previous experience working within a school or educational setting.
- Knowledge of school management information systems.
- Experience of attendance and financial administration.

4. Welsh Government Framework and Professional Expectations

The postholder is expected to demonstrate professional behaviours that support the school's wider educational priorities, particularly:
- Collaboration: Working effectively with colleagues, families and external partners.
- Professional Learning: Engaging in training, reflection and continuous development.
- Innovation: Identifying opportunities to improve administrative systems and processes.
- Leadership: Demonstrating initiative, accountability and professionalism within the role.
- Pedagogy and learner-centred practice: Supporting an effective school environment in which all learners can thrive.

5. Safeguarding

The school is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. All staff are expected to share this commitment and undertake appropriate safeguarding training. Appointment will be subject to satisfactory pre-employment checks, including an appropriate DBS check.
